candidate.answerReason: Both swimmers cover half the pool in \(1\tfrac12\) minutes, reach opposite ends at three minutes, and meet again \(1\tfrac12\) minutes later.

methods.label: Track successive half-lengths
methods.explanation:
Because they first meet at the center, each swimmer covers half the pool in \(1\tfrac12\) minutes. They cover equal distances in equal times, so their maintained speeds are equal.

After passing, they swim apart. Each takes another \(1\tfrac12\) minutes to reach the opposite end, arriving at three minutes after the start. They turn immediately and swim toward each other, meeting at the center after another \(1\tfrac12\) minutes. There is no intervening meeting while they are swimming apart.

The second meeting occurs at
\[
3+1\tfrac12=\boxed{4\tfrac12\text{ minutes}},
\]
choice B.
methods.levelReason: The argument uses constant-speed travel and equal-distance timing without requiring an equation.

candidate.annotationRationale: The target is the timing of a repeated meeting with immediate turns. The method uses the distance-speed-time relationship to track each half-pool journey; a linear-equation modeling procedure is not used.
